$schema_note: Severity ladder for AUDIT-10 findings. Severity is justified by the consequence to one of the two protected people (GUARDRAILS §0): Rick the owner, or a buyer looking for a spec-grade part. Never by how 'wrong' the code looks.

A.name: breaks an outcome
A.definition: costs a lead, destroys owner input, shows false product/certification information, renders a page unusable, or damages credibility in a way a buyer would notice and act on
examples: a save that silently deletes owner content
a page that does not render at a supported viewport
wrong SKU/spec shown for a part

B.name: real defect, will be hit and noticed
B.definition: wrong or misleading behavior a real visitor or Rick will encounter in normal use, but with a workaround or limited blast radius
examples: broken image frame on a reachable URL spelling
a control that works but misstates what it did

C.name: polish
C.definition: visibly imperfect but not misleading: misalignment, uneven spacing, inconsistent component treatment, awkward wrap, sub-AA-large contrast on decorative text
C.requires: at least LIKELY + a measurement (px, ratio, count) + issue screenshot

D.name: observation / nit
D.definition: a character-level or token-level inconsistency a meticulous reviewer records but no visitor would consciously notice: straight-vs-curly quote drift, a double space, a 1px radius difference, an off-scale margin used once
D.requires: the exact string/value and where it renders; batch related nits into ONE finding with an instances[] list rather than one record each
D.note: D exists so hyper-meticulous sweeps do not inflate C. A hundred D-nits must not drown three real Cs.

rules: severity A and B require confidence=CONFIRMED; an INFERRED record caps at C
when torn between two levels, pick the lower and say why in the severity_rationale field
an issue that only manifests on an unreachable state (URL the site never emits AND no external path to it) drops one level
known_issues in guardrails.json are never findings at any severity
